benchmarks.benchmark: CBO 2020 single-payer options: change in federal subsidies (corners reproduce the range)
benchmarks.note: Corners use only the payment-rate, cost-sharing and long-term-care assumptions the register gives (EV-CAR-220); CBO option specifications are not saved.
benchmarks.target: 1,660 to 3,319 $B (CBO $1.5-3.0T in 2030, grown to 2032 at CBO subsidy growth)
benchmarks.tolerance: each corner inside the range or within 25% of the nearer end

benchmarks.benchmark: CBO 2020 single-payer options: change in national health expenditures
benchmarks.note: CBO also changes provider supply and uses its 2020 baseline; the model grows both ends of the range to 2032.
benchmarks.target: -778 to 333 $B (CBO -$0.7T to +$0.3T in 2030, grown at NHE growth)
benchmarks.tolerance: each corner inside the range or within 25% of the nearer end

benchmarks.benchmark: P.L. 119-21: about 10 million more uninsured in 2034 (restoring the law provisions reverses it)
benchmarks.note: In-sample by construction: the restore flows are set from these same CBO estimates (7.5 million Medicaid, 2.8-2.9 million marketplace). The test checks the phase-in and band arithmetic, not an independent estimate.
benchmarks.target: 10.0 million (2034); 9.4 million on the 2029-34 CBO path interpolated to 2032

benchmarks.benchmark: Enhanced credits permanent: 3.8 million more insured
benchmarks.note: In-sample by construction (flow set from CBO).

benchmarks.benchmark: Enhanced credits permanent: about $350 billion over ten years (2032 annual cost against the ten-year average, shaped by CBO PTC growth)
benchmarks.note: Independent of the coverage inputs. The model prices new enrollees, repricing of existing enrollees and removal of the 400% cliff at CBO-calibrated premiums; it has no risk-pool premium reduction or employer-coverage offset.
benchmarks.target: 37.5 $B ($350B over 2026-35, spread on the PTC profile)

benchmarks.benchmark: P.L. 119-21 Medicaid provisions cut federal outlays $989.7 billion over FY2025-34 (restore reverses it)
benchmarks.note: The model restores only the coverage-linked cost unless mcd_financing_restore is raised; CBO also counts provider-tax and state-directed-payment cuts.

Unverified target: the 7.3 million is CBO 2022 as cited in the legacy memo (legacy/sources/health-working-group-memo-analysis.md, line 420); the saved CBO text (SRC-3204) gives shares, not this count. The model counts uninsured, nongroup and ESI people who move to Medicare; it does not count people who add Part A while keeping employer coverage.
benchmarks.target: 7.3 million (spec target; the saved CBO text gives shares, not this count)

benchmarks.benchmark: Urban 2019 single-payer federal cost (secondary): rise in federal spending relative to current federal health spending
benchmarks.note: Indicative only: Urban's baseline is not in the register, so RAND's federal base (EV-CAR-229) stands in; the model also counts the tax exclusion.
benchmarks.target: 138% (Urban lite, $1.5T in 2020) to 257% (enhanced, $2.8T), on RAND's $1,090B 2019 federal base
benchmarks.tolerance: inside the range or within 25% of an end

benchmarks.benchmark: Urban 2019 hybrid reform with a public option (secondary): federal cost relative to current federal health spending
benchmarks.note: Urban's bundle adds a mandate and rate caps and covers fewer people than restore plus public option; not a like-for-like test.
